files.insight: Global clone ranking can allocate two choices to f and none to g even with max-clones=1, since the budget is multiplied by eligible functions. Ink should distinguish global family allocation from strict per-function limits; benefits still require target evidence.

Unprofitable speculative analyses must not consume permanent growth budget or prevent a later profitable specialization. The expected poison return depends on unused-return LLVM semantics; never import it as an Ink equality.

Repeated call sites with the same ordered specialized argument signature reuse a clone; different signatures and partially bound recursive calls are rematched. Ink keys must bind exact source/context and proofs rather than only helper names.
